exercise.name: Dumbbell Deep Push-up and Renegade Row

reference.title: Dumbbell Deep Push-up and Renegade Row
reference.listing: Page could not be read (blocked by the network proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.laterality: Bilateral push-up, alternating rows (right then left in one loop)

breathing.pattern: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you push up; exhale on each row, inhale as you set the dumbbell down.
breathing.cadence: Push-up about 1.4 s down, 1 s up; each row about 1 s up, 1 s down

prescription.reps: 5-8 cycles (one push-up and one row per arm)
prescription.load: Hex dumbbells that sit flat (round ones can roll). Pick a weight you can row for the target reps with 2-3 reps in reserve (RIR 2-3) without the hips twisting.
prescription.progression: Add cycles, then heavier dumbbells; slow the lowering of the push-up.

cues.text: High plank gripping two hex dumbbells under the shoulders, handles along the body, feet wide on the balls of the feet, body in one straight line.
Breathe in and lower the chest between the dumbbells, below the level of the hands, elbows about 45 degrees from the body.
Breathe out and push back up to straight arms, the body moving as one piece.
Brace, push the left dumbbell into the floor and row the right one to the lower ribs, elbow close; hips stay square to the floor.
Set the dumbbell down softly under the shoulder.
Re-brace in the plank; row the other side, then start the next push-up.

mistakes.mistake: Hips sagging in the deep push-up
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and brace the abs; keep the body in one line.
Widen the feet and push the supporting dumbbell into the floor.

mistakes.mistake: Going deeper than the shoulders allow
mistakes.fix: Stop where the shoulders are comfortable; the chest only needs to pass the hands.
Use hex dumbbells so they cannot roll under the hands.
Pause briefly at the top and set the dumbbell down softly.

kinematics.setup: Trunk 30.8° above the floor, 14° off a straight shoulder-hip-ankle line
kinematics.peak: Held straight through the push-up and the rows
kinematics.norm: Shoulders, hips and ankles in one line throughout (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Chest 51.6 cm above the floor, arms straight
kinematics.peak: Chest 18 cm above the floor: 0.5 cm above the wrists, 8 cm above the handles, between the dumbbells; elbows ≈139°
kinematics.norm: Raised handles allow the chest to drop below the hands for a longer range than a floor push-up (clinical opinion)
Straight arm with the dumbbell on the floor; about 90 degrees or more at the top of the row (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Ankles 38 cm apart; dumbbell handles 44 cm apart
kinematics.norm: Feet wider than the hips for a stable base during the rows (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Push-up 1.4 s down, 1 s up; each row 1 s up, 1 s down
kinematics.norm: Controlled push-up, brief squeeze at the top of each row (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #16362, Dumbbell Deep Push-up and Renegade Row, video (movement reference; page not readable here)
Kim, Kim and Ha 2016, effect of the push-up exercise at different palmar width on muscle activities (J Phys Ther Sci 28(2):446-449; PMC4792988)
Fenwick, Brown & McGill 2009, comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load and stiffness (J Strength Cond Res 23(2):350-358)
Escamilla et al. 2016, muscle activation among supine, prone and side position exercises with and without a Swiss ball (Sports Health 8(4):372-379)

cautions: Use hex dumbbells on a non-slip floor; round dumbbells can roll out from under the hands.
Keep the wrists straight over the handles; stop if the wrists hurt.
Shoulder discomfort at the bottom: reduce the depth to a regular push-up.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knees down for the push-up and the rows.
Push-up on the floor, then the rows.
progressions: Slower lowering (3 s) in the push-up.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pusher in the deep push-up; push-up hand placement changes pectoralis activity (Kim 2016).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbow in the push-up and keeps the supporting arm straight during the row.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the dumbbell back toward the hip in the row.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blade back at the top of the row.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Extends the shoulder in the row.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bend the elbow in the row.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Hold the shoulder blade on the rib cage in the plank.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the plank; rowing from a plank asked much more of the trunk muscles than supported rows (Fenwick 2009).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the trunk rotating as one hand leaves the floor.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the trunk rotating as one hand leaves the floor.
